data.content_ref: inline:The target argues the panel is LESS reliable because checklists miss edge cases, but the problem asks which is MORE reliable ON AVERAGE for tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes. The target's own mechanism concedes the panel achieves high checklist compliance on ~95% of cases and only fails on the complex 5%. For objectively verifiable outcomes, higher accuracy on the majority of cases IS higher average reliability. The target provides no evidence that the 5% edge-case failures outweigh the compliance gains on the 95%—yet concludes the panel is less reliable overall. This is internally inconsistent with averaging over verifiable outcomes. A panel that is right more often on average is more reliable on average, even if it loses specific edge-case sensitivity.
